Market research firm Counterpoint Research's latest report shows that Apple surpassed Samsung in European telecom operator sales channels in the second quarter of 2026, becoming the leading smartphone brand in the region, as telecom operator sales outperformed the overall market. Details below.

Apple drives telecom operator sales to outperform the European smartphone market

A report released today by Counterpoint Research indicates that smartphones sold through European telecom operators in the second quarter of 2026 fell 4% year-on-year, compared with an 11% drop in the open market. The report shows that overall smartphone sales declined 8% year-on-year.

Counterpoint said this once again reflects the impact of rising memory costs, with the European low-end smartphone market being hit particularly hard. Telecom operator channel sales performed relatively better because their customer base tends to purchase higher-end devices bought on contract and high-end brands such as Apple.

The report noted that Apple's share of European telecom operator smartphone sales rose from 33% in the second quarter of 2025 to 37% in the second quarter of 2026; over the same period, Samsung fell from 39% to 34%.

However, in terms of year-on-year growth, Chinese brand vivo saw the largest increase in telecom operator sales, reaching 90%; Motorola trailed far behind in second place with 27% growth.

Below is a response from Counterpoint Research Associate Director Jan Stryjak on the data:

Stryjak added that he expects the telecom operator channel to continue gaining market share over the "next few quarters," as the "low-end market continues to be affected by the memory crisis." He also pointed out that independent retailers have stepped up promotional efforts, which "may ease some of the pricing pressure compared with telecom operators and bring additional stimulus to the open market."
